context.join: requirements[].name is the requirement name every claim in generated/requirements.json is judged against; the join is total in both directions
context.statements: statements[] are the design decisions and assumptions no numeric claim is judged against, including the choices that close the brief's open questions

requirements.name: assembly_within_declared_policy
requirements.rationale: the brief puts the connectors, the button and the indicators on one face; what that costs at assembly is a count of sides and of hand operations, and it should be a measurement rather than an intention
requirements.statement: the board is assembled the way its declared policy says

requirements.name: both_orientations_terminated
requirements.statement: the input works with the plug either way round

requirements.name: button_current_below_contact_rating
requirements.rationale: the switch is rated for a signal contact, not a supply one, and the board pulls its node up
requirements.statement: the current through the button's contacts stays below its rating

requirements.name: button_filter_below_ignore_window
requirements.rationale: the brief requires the button debounced. The controller debounces in time; the filter exists for noise and static, and must not eat the window that debounce depends on
requirements.statement: the filter across the button settles well inside the window the controller ignores a press shorter than

requirements.name: cell_connector_polarised
requirements.rationale: the brief requires a reversed cell to leave the board undamaged. The protection device's own supply pin sits across the cell, and a reversed cell drives it below its absolute minimum, so the reversal is prevented mechanically rather than survived electrically
requirements.statement: the cell connector is keyed so the cell cannot be fitted reversed

requirements.name: cell_connector_within_current_rating
requirements.rationale: the brief makes cell-side current the figure that sizes conductors, and the connector is one of them
requirements.statement: the cell connector carries less than its rated current at the worst-case cell current

requirements.name: cell_rail_parts_rated_above_protection_ceiling
requirements.rationale: the brief requires parts on the battery rail to be rated above its maximum. That maximum is not the charger's target: it is the highest voltage that can stand on the rail before something intervenes, which is the protection's own over-charge threshold at the top of its tolerance
requirements.statement: every part on the cell rail is rated above the highest voltage the protection device permits the cell to reach

requirements.name: charger_input_above_undervoltage_lockout
requirements.rationale: the brief requires operation over the whole vSafe5V range; a series switch drops voltage, and below the lockout the charger stops
requirements.statement: the charger's input stays above the controller's undervoltage lockout with the input switch conducting its worst-case current at the bottom of the declared source range

requirements.name: clamp_working_voltage_above_rail
requirements.rationale: a clamp below the rail conducts continuously, which is a fault rather than protection
requirements.statement: every clamp's reverse stand-off voltage is at least the highest steady voltage on the conductor it protects

requirements.name: comparator_input_within_common_mode_range
requirements.rationale: outside the common-mode range a comparator's output is not defined by its inputs, so the threshold claim would rest on nothing
requirements.statement: the highest CC voltage the detector must resolve stays inside the comparator's input common-mode range at the lowest supply

requirements.name: conductor_width_for_cell_current
requirements.rationale: the brief requires conductor cross-sections to meet a stated temperature-rise limit at worst-case cell-side current. Before there is copper to measure, the declared net-class width is what the requirement applies to
requirements.statement: the conductor width the board declares for its power nets carries the worst-case cell current inside the declared temperature rise

requirements.name: connector_contract_consistent
requirements.rationale: a receptacle that mates mechanically but carries the wrong net on VBUS or CC is the one mistake the connector itself cannot prevent
requirements.statement: every connector pin carries the net its function names

requirements.name: converter_junction_below_thermal_shutdown
requirements.rationale: the brief requires the rated output sustained in still air with no thermal foldback; foldback for this device is its own thermal shutdown, so the requirement is a junction temperature below that threshold rather than a generic derating
requirements.statement: the converter's junction stays below its thermal shutdown threshold delivering the rated output in still air at room ambient

requirements.name: esd_coverage_complete
requirements.statement: every conductor that enters the board at a user-accessible connector is clamped

requirements.name: indicator_current_within_rating
requirements.rationale: the state-of-charge indicators are driven by a current source inside the controller and the fault indicator by a series resistor, so the two are bounded differently
requirements.statement: every indicator carries less than its rated forward current

requirements.name: indicator_reverse_within_rating
requirements.rationale: four indicators are driven from three pins as antiparallel pairs, so lighting one reverse-biases the other by that one's forward voltage
requirements.statement: an indicator held off by the drive that lights its pair sees less reverse voltage than it is rated for

requirements.name: inductor_peak_below_saturation
requirements.rationale: the brief makes cell-side current the figure that sizes magnetics. For an inductor that figure is the peak, not the average: ripple at the declared switching frequency is a large fraction of the average at this inductance
requirements.statement: the peak inductor current at the rated output and the lowest cell voltage stays below the inductor's saturation current

requirements.name: inductor_rms_below_heat_rating
requirements.rationale: saturation and self-heating are separate limits and the smaller one decides
requirements.statement: the RMS inductor current at the rated output stays below the inductor's heat rating current

requirements.name: input_current_below_advertisement
requirements.statement: the board draws no more from the source than the source advertises

requirements.name: input_ring_below_clamp_breakdown
requirements.rationale: a step through a series inductance into a capacitance overshoots, and plugging a charger in is that step. The clamp on that conductor is there for electrostatic discharge, not for an event that happens every time the board is used, so the ring has to stay below the voltage at which the clamp starts to conduct
requirements.statement: connecting a live source through a cable's inductance does not ring the input above the clamp's breakdown voltage

requirements.name: input_switch_junction_below_maximum
requirements.rationale: the input switch carries the whole charge current in a small package
requirements.statement: the input switch's junction stays below its rated maximum at the highest input current the controller is specified for and the declared maximum ambient

requirements.name: kelvin_pairs_present
requirements.statement: the cell side, the output and the reference each carry a pair of probes so current and voltage can be measured separately

requirements.name: latch_hold_capacitor_rated_above_set_level
requirements.rationale: the feedback divider is fed from the converter output, which is higher than the cell rail every other part of the latch sees
requirements.statement: the latch's hold capacitor is rated above the highest voltage its feedback can put on it

requirements.name: latch_hold_level_above_threshold
requirements.rationale: without the feedback the latch would release the moment the button did
requirements.statement: the latch's own feedback holds its gate above the switching device's highest gate threshold once the output is up

requirements.name: latch_hold_time_above_target
requirements.rationale: the feedback comes from the output, and at the instant of the press the output is not up yet. The controller's datasheet states no start-up time, so the latch has to bridge an interval this design declares rather than one a document gives
requirements.statement: the latch holds its set state for longer than the declared converter start-up allowance with no feedback

requirements.name: latch_set_level_above_threshold
requirements.rationale: the enable is a latch and the press is what sets it; below the gate threshold the press does nothing
requirements.statement: a held button drives the latch's gate above the switching device's highest gate threshold, at the lowest cell voltage

requirements.name: no_floating_node
requirements.statement: the button presents no floating node

requirements.name: output_advertisement_lands_in_3_0A_band
requirements.rationale: the output port advertises by presenting a pull-up, and what a sink reads is the divider between that pull-up and the sink's own termination; the advertisement is only made if the result lands in the band
requirements.statement: a sink attached to the output port reads a CC voltage inside the band the specification defines for a 3.0 A advertisement

requirements.name: output_holds_through_response_budget
requirements.rationale: the converter has no vendor model and its datasheet states no loop response time, so the output capacitance is sized against a declared budget instead. The level the dip has to stay above is not declared: it is the one the converter's own load-overcurrent detector uses
requirements.statement: the output capacitance alone holds the port above the level the converter treats as an overload, for as long as this design allows the converter's loop to take to answer a step to the rated current

requirements.name: output_off_until_a_press
requirements.statement: the output is off when a cell is attached and after a protection event, and only a button press enables it

requirements.name: output_switch_junction_below_maximum
requirements.rationale: the enable switch carries the whole output current in a small package
requirements.statement: the output enable switch's junction stays below its rated maximum at the rated output and the declared maximum ambient

requirements.name: package_pins_match_land_pattern
requirements.rationale: a simulation and a requirement report can both be right about a part whose footprint has a pad the schematic never names
requirements.statement: every symbol's pin count equals its land pattern's pad count

requirements.name: parts_rated_above_rail_maximum
requirements.rationale: the brief bounds the input by the Type-C vSafe5V range; the top of that range is what parts on the input side see
requirements.statement: every part on a 5 V rail is rated above the highest voltage that rail can reach

requirements.name: port_connector_within_current_rating
requirements.rationale: the same figure applies to the receptacles the current enters and leaves by
requirements.statement: each port carries less than its receptacle's rated current

requirements.name: port_voltage_above_source_minimum
requirements.rationale: the board is a source at that port; the specification's pull-up table is stated for a supply of 4.75 V to 5.5 V, so an output that sagged below 4.75 V would invalidate the advertisement as well as the rating
requirements.statement: the voltage at the output port at the rated current stays above the lowest a Type-C source may present

requirements.name: probe_access_complete
requirements.statement: every net the brief requires a probe on reaches one

requirements.name: protection_does_not_trip_at_rated_output
requirements.rationale: the brief makes cell-side current at rated output and minimum cell voltage the figure that sets over-current margin. The protection senses a voltage across the switch, so its trip current is set by the switch's resistance, and a trip during normal operation is a functional failure rather than a safety action
requirements.statement: the cell protection's lowest over-current trip current is above the highest instantaneous cell current the rated output produces

requirements.name: protection_overcharge_above_charge_target
requirements.rationale: the two devices are independent, so the protection must sit outside the charger's own regulation or it will cut a normal charge short
requirements.statement: the protection's lowest over-charge threshold is above the voltage the charger terminates at

requirements.name: protection_overdischarge_below_operating_floor
requirements.rationale: the protection is a backstop for a fault, not the working cut-off; if it tripped first the pack would need a charger to recover from an ordinary discharge
requirements.statement: the protection's highest over-discharge threshold is below the lowest cell voltage the converter operates at

requirements.name: protection_switch_junction_below_maximum
requirements.rationale: conduction loss in the switch is the largest dissipation on the cell rail and the package is small
requirements.statement: the protection switch's junction stays below its rated maximum at the worst-case cell current and the declared maximum ambient

requirements.name: protection_switch_within_current_rating
requirements.rationale: the packages share the cell current; the share, not the total, is what each package is rated against
requirements.statement: each protection switch package carries less than its rated continuous drain current at the worst-case cell current

requirements.name: rated_output_current_supported
requirements.statement: the board delivers at least the rated current at 5 V across the whole usable cell voltage range

requirements.name: reference_bias_above_regulation_minimum
requirements.rationale: the threshold is only as good as the reference behind it, and a shunt reference below its minimum cathode current is not regulating at all
requirements.statement: the shunt reference carries at least the cathode current it needs to regulate, at the lowest input the board accepts

requirements.name: reference_bias_below_maximum
requirements.rationale: the same bias resistor sets both ends
requirements.statement: the shunt reference's cathode current stays inside its rating at the highest input the board accepts

requirements.name: reference_load_capacitance_within_stable_range
requirements.rationale: a shunt reference is a feedback loop; the datasheet's stability boundary is stated for the cathode-tied-to-reference connection this board uses, so it is a figure rather than a judgement
requirements.statement: the capacitance across the reference is inside the range the datasheet states the device is stable into

requirements.name: rejected_source_current_below_default
requirements.rationale: the board answers a weak source by not charging, but the detector itself runs from the source; what it draws has to be inside the default advertisement or the refusal is not a refusal
requirements.statement: with the advertisement below what the board requires, the current it takes from the source stays under the smallest advertisement a Type-C source can make

requirements.name: sink_termination_within_specification
requirements.rationale: the brief says the input 'presents the sink CC terminations Type-C requires'. Which termination that is depends on whether the sink reads the advertisement: this one does, and the specification's table permits +/-10% for that case and +/-20% for a sink that does not
requirements.statement: each CC conductor of the input port is terminated by a resistance inside the tolerance the Type-C specification allows a sink that reads the source's current advertisement

requirements.name: standby_current_below_self_discharge
requirements.statement: the current the board takes from the cell with the output off and no source attached is small against the cell's own self-discharge

requirements.name: stock_covers_planned_build
requirements.rationale: a design that cannot be built is not finished; the catalogue snapshot is frozen so this is a statement about a recorded state rather than about today's web page
requirements.statement: every part is stocked in at least the quantity the planned build needs

requirements.name: switch_gate_slew_above_target
requirements.rationale: a switch that closes instantly charges the capacitance behind it from the capacitance in front of it; the brief's inrush and high-current-loop requirements are easier to meet if the switch is the thing that limits it
requirements.statement: each switch's gate network takes at least the declared time to turn the switch on

requirements.name: switch_gate_within_rating
requirements.rationale: both switches are driven between a rail and ground rather than through a clamp, so the rail's own maximum is the gate stress
requirements.statement: neither switch's gate-source voltage exceeds its rating in any state the board can reach

requirements.name: threshold_above_1_5A_advertisement
requirements.rationale: the board takes more current than a 1.5 A source offers, so it must not mistake that advertisement for the 3.0 A one. The specification tabulates the sink-side voltage bands directly, and the bands - not the pull-up tolerances - are what a threshold has to clear
requirements.statement: the detector's threshold sits above every CC voltage a source advertising 1.5 A can produce at this sink

requirements.name: threshold_below_3_0A_advertisement
requirements.rationale: a threshold above the 3.0 A band would reject every source and the board would never charge; the band's lower edge is what it has to stay under
requirements.statement: the detector's threshold sits below every CC voltage a source advertising 3.0 A can produce at this sink

alternatives_considered: drawing the controller's full charge current from any source, rejected because it violates the brief against every source that advertises less
a fixed current limiter set to the default advertisement, rejected because a limiter in constant-current mode drops the input below the controller's lockout and the pair hiccups
reading the advertisement and selecting between two limits, rejected as more parts than the added charge rate is worth on a board whose charge current is an open choice
statements.name: advertisement_gated_charging
statements.rationale: the brief requires the board to draw no more than the source advertises, and the controller has no input current limit that can be set from outside. Gating the whole charger input on the advertisement makes the requirement a property of the hardware rather than of the controller's behaviour
statements.statement: the board charges only from a source that advertises 3.0 A, and takes nothing but its detector's own current from any weaker one

statements.invalidated_by: a measured efficiency below 85% at the rated output and 3.0 V, which would raise the cell current and could put it above the protection's lowest trip current
statements.name: boost_efficiency_floor
statements.reason: the cell-side current, and with it the protection margin, the inductor rating and every conductor width, is computed from the output power and this efficiency. The controller's datasheet states a peak efficiency and no minimum, so the floor is this board's
statements.statement: the converter is at least 85% efficient delivering the rated output from the lowest usable cell voltage

statements.invalidated_by: a measured capacitance below the declared fraction, which would shorten the latch's hold and the button filter's settling
statements.name: capacitor_dc_bias
statements.reason: every capacitance figure in the latch timing and the filter timing depends on it. The datasheets state the effect as a curve this repository has not digitised, so the fraction is declared rather than read
statements.statement: class II ceramic capacitors retain the declared fraction of their nominal capacitance at the DC bias this board applies

statements.invalidated_by: a cell whose self-discharge is lower than this, which would make the board's standby current the larger of the two
statements.name: cell_self_discharge
statements.reason: the brief judges standby current against the cell's self-discharge and neither names a cell nor states a rate; the comparison needs both numbers and this repository freezes no cell datasheet
statements.statement: the cell loses 2% of a 2 Ah capacity per month to self-discharge

alternatives_considered: three indicators on three pins, rejected because the datasheet's three-indicator table resolves the charge state more coarsely
a separate indicator driver, rejected as parts spent on something the controller already does
statements.name: charlieplexed_indicators
statements.rationale: the controller's pin table brings out three indicator drivers and its indication tables describe a four-indicator display; its own reference application resolves that by pairing the indicators across the drivers, and this board wires them the same way rather than choosing the three-indicator mode and losing a level
statements.statement: four state-of-charge indicators are driven from three controller pins as two antiparallel pairs

alternatives_considered: a fixed rule of thumb in amps per millimetre, rejected because it hides the temperature rise it assumes
a thermal solve, rejected as more than this stage's evidence supports
statements.name: conductor_sizing_model
statements.rationale: the brief requires conductors to meet a stated temperature-rise limit and states no limit. The relation is manufacturer-independent and the rise is this board's declaration
statements.statement: conductor cross-sections are sized by the IPC-2221 external-layer current capacity relation at a 20 degC rise

statements.invalidated_by: a measured input current above the recommended maximum, which would break the advertisement claim rather than any rating
statements.name: controller_stays_inside_recommended_input
statements.reason: the board has no independent limiter between the input switch and the charger, so the claim that it stays inside the advertisement rests on the device staying inside its own recommended conditions
statements.statement: the controller draws no more from its input than the maximum load current its recommended operating conditions state

alternatives_considered: sizing the capacitance for a millisecond, rejected because holding the rated current for that long would need nearly two orders more capacitance than the converter's own reference design carries
not sizing it at all and relying on the converter, rejected because nothing in the frozen evidence says what the converter does during a step
statements.name: converter_response_budget
statements.rationale: the datasheet states a switching frequency and no loop response time, and the output capacitance cannot be sized without one. Five periods is what a current-mode converter of this class needs to act on a load step, and it is stated here rather than assumed silently
statements.statement: the converter's control loop is allowed ten microseconds - five switching periods - to answer a step to the rated output current

statements.invalidated_by: a measured case temperature that implies a higher thermal resistance, which would raise the junction temperature at the rated output
statements.name: converter_thermal_resistance
statements.reason: the datasheet gives one figure and does not say what board it was measured on. Every junction temperature for that device rests on it
statements.statement: the controller's stated junction-to-ambient thermal resistance applies to this board's copper

alternatives_considered: relying on the controller's own stated protections, rejected because they are inside the device whose failure they would have to survive
a protection device with an external sense resistor, rejected because the sense resistor would dissipate the cell current continuously
statements.name: independent_cell_protection
statements.rationale: the brief requires those protections to hold with any programmable device unpowered or unprogrammed. A protection that shares a die with the converter shares its failure modes; one that runs from the cell and switches the cell's own return does not
statements.statement: cell over-voltage, under-voltage, over-current and short-circuit protection is a separate analogue device in the cell's negative leg, not a function of the controller

alternatives_considered: no fault indicator, rejected because the brief asks for one
an indicator driven from the protection device, rejected because a protection trip disconnects the return everything on the board is referenced to
statements.name: input_rejected_indicator
statements.rationale: the brief asks the indication to separate charge state, charging, charge complete and fault. The controller's own indicators cover the first three. Of the faults this board can have, the only one it can both detect and still be powered to show is a source it has refused: a protection trip removes the board's own reference and a converter shutdown removes its supply, so neither can light anything
statements.statement: the fault indicator shows one condition: a source is attached and its advertisement is below what the board requires

alternatives_considered: a discrete buck charger, a discrete boost converter and a power-path switch, rejected because the arbitration between them would be this board's own design and nothing in the datasheets would establish it
a charger with an I2C-controlled boost, rejected because the output would then depend on firmware, and the brief requires the protections to hold with any programmable device unprogrammed
statements.name: integrated_controller
statements.rationale: the brief prefers an integrated solution where practical. One device with one inductor removes the power-path arbitration between a separate charger and a separate boost, which is the part of this architecture that is hardest to get right and hardest to verify from datasheets alone
statements.statement: charger, power path, boost converter and state-of-charge indication are one integrated controller rather than discrete stages

alternatives_considered: evaluating everything at room ambient, rejected because a rating that only holds on a bench is not a rating
the controller's own 70 degC maximum ambient, rejected because at that ambient the converter's junction claim has no margin left for the thermal resistance assumption below it
statements.name: maximum_ambient
statements.rationale: the brief conditions its thermal requirement on 'still air at room ambient' and states no figure for the rating case. Every junction temperature here is computed at one of the two, and which one is stated with the claim
statements.statement: the board's ratings are claimed at a maximum ambient of 40 degC, and the sustained-output requirement is evaluated at 25 degC

statements.invalidated_by: a first article whose output is live at cell attach behind the enable switch, which would not change the port's behaviour but would change what the board dissipates while idle
statements.name: power_on_output_state
statements.reason: the controller's datasheet states what a short press and a long press do, and states neither the converter's state when a cell is first attached nor whether its integrated load detector enables the converter unprompted. The board does not depend on the answer - the enable switch is what holds the port off - but the claim that the converter itself is off is not established
statements.statement: the converter does not enable its output without a button press

alternatives_considered: one package, rejected because its lowest trip current is below the average cell current at the rated output
two packages, rejected because the margin over the peak is smaller than the ripple the inductance produces
a protection device with a higher sense threshold, which would need one package - none of the ones stocked for a single cell offers one
statements.name: protection_switch_count
statements.rationale: the protection senses a voltage across the switch, so the switch's resistance sets the trip current. One package would trip below the rated output and two would leave the trip current inside the ripple; three puts the lowest trip current clear of the highest instantaneous cell current
statements.statement: three switch packages carry the cell current in parallel

statements.invalidated_by: a measured turn-off time long enough that the short-circuit current exceeds the switch's pulsed rating before it opens
statements.name: protection_turn_off_time
statements.reason: the datasheet characterises the gate outputs only at 10 uA, so the current available to discharge the parallel gates - and with it the time between detection and the current actually stopping - is not established
statements.statement: the protection device turns its switch off inside the delay its datasheet states for the detection

alternatives_considered: a factor of two below the self-discharge, rejected because the controller's own standby current alone exceeds it
a larger cell or a higher self-discharge rate, rejected because either would make the requirement easier without evidence
statements.name: small_against_self_discharge
statements.rationale: the brief compares two currents and quantifies neither. The cell is not part of this design, so both numbers are declared: 2.5 Ah is the low end of a single cell of the size this board is built around and 2% per month the low end of the usual band, which together make the comparison the hardest rather than the easiest. A stricter reading - a factor below the self-discharge - would be a requirement no integrated controller of this class meets, because the controller's own standby current is the whole of the board's and cannot be reduced from outside it
statements.statement: 'small against the cell's self-discharge' is read as 'not larger than it', against a 2.5 Ah cell losing 2% of its charge per month

alternatives_considered: a Standard-A receptacle, rejected because the ones available are rated at 1.5 A and the board is rated at 2 A
a conforming Type-C source with attach detection, rejected as a second comparator, a second reference and a two-input enable for a port whose only function is to deliver 5 V
statements.name: type_c_output_port
statements.rationale: the rated output current exceeds what a Standard-A receptacle is rated to carry, and the Type-C receptacle is rated well above it. The board does not implement Type-C attach detection: it presents the pull-up and energises the port on the user's press, so it is a charging port that advertises correctly rather than a conforming source, and no compliance claim is made for it
statements.statement: the output is a Type-C receptacle presenting a source pull-up, and the board applies VBUS when the user enables the output rather than when it detects a sink

alternatives_considered: a range taken from a nominated cell, rejected because nominating a cell would put a document this repository does not hold under every rail claim
statements.name: usable_cell_range
statements.rationale: the brief makes the battery rail span the cell's discharge cut-off to its maximum charge voltage. The cell is not part of this design and no cell datasheet is frozen here, so the range the board can actually claim is the one its converter is specified over, which is narrower than any cell's
statements.statement: the usable cell voltage range is the controller's own battery operating range, 3.0 V to the charger's 4.2 V termination

alternatives_considered: allowing a via inside a pad and ordering a filled-and-capped process, rejected because it prices the whole board for the handful of vias that wanted it
leaving the contact and relying on the mask to bridge it, rejected because mask over an annulus that touches an opening is a sliver rather than a tent, and the fabricator is free to drop it
statements.name: vias_clear_of_solder_mask_openings
statements.rationale: a via whose annulus reaches an opening cannot be tented or plugged, so its barrel is open to whatever the assembly puts on the opening beside it; where that opening is one a paste aperture fills, the joint's own solder wicks into the barrel and leaves the joint short of it. The board carries the distance as a rule the placement searches its stitches against, the search is given the same figure, and a routed board that still has one is refused, so it is a property of the board rather than something a review would have to notice
statements.statement: no via's annulus reaches a pad's solder-mask opening
